instrument_info.nama: Big Five Personality Questionnaire - Short Version (Mini-IPIP, 20 items)
referensi_utama: Donnellan, M. B., Oswald, F. L., Baird, B. M., & Lucas, R. E. (2006). The Mini-IPIP scales: Tiny-yet-effective measures of the Big Five factors of personality. Psychological Assessment, 18(2), 192-203.
International Personality Item Pool (IPIP). Mini-IPIP Scoring Key. Retrieved from https://ipip.ori.org/MiniIPIPKey.htm — items are public domain.
instrument_info.catatan_metodologis: Mini-IPIP is a concise version of the IPIP-50 developed to maximize reliability and cross-dimension independence despite having far fewer items (20 vs 50 items). The original study (Donnellan et al., 2006) reported adequate reliability and convergent validity for research and brief screening use.
instrument_info.instruksi: Read each statement below and choose the number 1-5 that best describes you in general.

big_five_questionnaire.statement: I usually liven up the atmosphere when gathering with others.
I sympathize with others' feelings.
I try to complete tasks as soon as I have the opportunity.
I have frequent mood swings.
I often have many ideas or imagine various possibilities.
I don't talk a lot.
I am not really interested in others.
I often forget to tidy up or organize things after using them.
I am relaxed most of the time.
I am less interested in thinking about complex ideas or concepts.
I talk to a lot of different people at parties.
I feel others' emotions.
I like order.
I get upset easily.
I have difficulty understanding complex concepts or those requiring a lot of thought.
I keep in the background.
I am not particularly interested in knowing what others think or feel.
I make a mess of things.
I seldom feel blue.
I feel like I don't have much imagination or many new ideas.

panduan_skoring.langkah_1: For items keyed '+', score = the answer value (1-5).
panduan_skoring.langkah_3: Average the 4 item scores per dimension (E, A, C, N, O) to get the final trait score (scale 1-5).
panduan_skoring.interpretasi_umum: Average scores near 5 indicate that trait is very prominent; near 1 indicates low trait presence. Scores around 3 indicate balanced/situational tendencies.
